newsitem.title: BRUNEI: Tiny Brunei says it will buy British fighter planes.
newsitem.headline: Tiny Brunei says it will buy British fighter planes.

text.p: The tiny oil sultanate of Brunei said on Thursday it would buy Hawk fighter planes from Britain under a multi-million dollar military deal to modernise the country's armed forces.
Brunei Sultan Hassanal Bolkiah discussed the purchase with visiting British Defence Secretary Michael Portillo, a Brunei palace communique issued after the meeting said.
Portillo declined to say how many of the fighter jets manufactured by British Aerospace Brunei would buy or how much money was involved.
But sources said it would be more than 30 planes.
Brunei's air force currently consists of a squadron of 13 helicopters and two fixed-wing aircraft.

Portillo said Brunei needs to decide where and how the new Hawk squadron would operate. There had been talk earlier of a need to build a new airfield in the interior of the country, away from the Malaysian border.
"Clearly, Brunei wants to buy the Hawks," Portillo told reporters. "But naturally Brunei needs to take some important decisions how these will be operating and from where.
"But today his Majesty and I agreed that this project is proceeding very well without any matters to discuss," he said.
Brunei shares its border with Malaysia on Borneo island.
Brunei has already bought two frigate-class patrol vessels built by Yarrow shipyard and General Electric Co Plc under a 1994 Brunei-Britain defence procurement agreement.
The armed forces also has a squadron of British-made Scorpion tanks, armoured personnel carriers and patrol boats armed with Exocet missiles.
